Apologist

uh-PAH-luh-jist · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Apologist is a person who argues in defense of something controversial, especially a cause, religion, or policy.

Historians criticized the biography for reading less like objective history and more like the work of an apologist for the fallen dictator.

Worked Example

Even as evidence of the company's pollution mounted, one loyal spokesperson remained its most tireless public apologist, defending every decision on television.

Defending something controversial, often no matter how much evidence stacks up against it, is exactly what apologist describes.

How Apologist Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

defender

defender: a person who argues in support of someone or something

champion: a person who vigorously supports or defends a cause

Antonyms

opponent

opponent: a person who is against something or someone

dissenter

dissenter: a person who publicly disagrees with an official or popular opinion

How Strong Is It? — defender → apologist → champion

defender vs. apologist

defender vs. apologist: Defender is milder than apologist: a defender calmly answers tough questions as they come, while an apologist argues more forcefully and persistently for a controversial cause.

champion vs. apologist

champion vs. apologist: Champion is stronger than apologist: an apologist argues in a cause's defense, but a champion goes further, personally funding projects and fighting to push the cause ahead.

Build the Word

The pieces

root — apo-

root — apo-: away, off, from (Greek)

root — -log-

root — -log-: speech, word, reason (Greek)

suffix — -ist

suffix — -ist: one who (Greek)

Put it together

Put it together: Apologist comes from Greek apologia, 'a speech in defense' -- apo- ('away, off') plus logos ('speech, reason') -- with -ist, 'one who.' An apologist is one who speaks in defense, pushing accusations away, which is also why the word looks so much like 'apology.'

Use the root in a new word: dialogue

Use the root in a new word: dialogue: The two rival mayors finally agreed to open a public dialogue about the disputed border.

Root Check

Word Choice

Apologist is a false friend for 'someone who apologizes' -- it actually means the opposite: a person who defends a controversial idea, cause, or figure, often stubbornly. The word almost always carries a critical edge when used about someone else, as in 'an apologist for the regime.'
